title: Lightweight incident cookbook: customer choices and status snippets
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, customer-oriented incident "decision cookbook" to speed status updates and post-incident summaries. Intended for CS and Ops to copy/paste into status pages, customer emails, and account-specific outreach. Focus: clarity, explicit choices for customers, and a short evidence checklist they can use to verify behavior.

When to use:
- Partial or progressive inference degradations that affect correctness or latency for a subset of tenants
- Short outages where customers may want to: opt into a replay, pin an earlier model, or accept a temporary degraded-mode while we remediate

TL;DR template (one-liner for status page):
- Immediate: "Investigating: elevated generation latency and intermittent truncated responses for some tenants. Engineering engaged; mitigation in progress."
- Update (30–90 min): "Partial recovery: region X routing moved to fallback model; customers on pinned models unaffected. Rolling verification and targeted replays available."
- Resolution: "Resolved: root cause patch deployed; optional tenant-guided replays offered. See postmortem for details and verification instructions."

Plain-language customer summary (short paragraph for emails):
On 2026-07-18, Redwood observed intermittent high-latency and a small number of truncated/partial outputs for requests routed to our serving cluster in us-west-2. The issue was caused by an interaction between caching eviction and a new kernel selection path for long-context requests. We diverted traffic to a compatible model variant, deployed a fix to the selection logic, and validated token-level integrity. No customer data was exposed. We are offering replay and reconciliation options for teams that need deterministic reprocessing.

Quick timeline (operator notes to include in status updates):
- 2026-07-18 09:12 UTC — Alerts triggered: sustained p50 latency spike on us-west-2 serving pool
- 09:20 UTC — Triage: identified correlation with requests >4k tokens using auto-kernel switch path
- 09:31 UTC — Traffic routing change: partial roll to fallback model variant for affected routes
- 09:50 UTC — Hotfix deployed to kernel selection flag; monitoring shows latency decline
- 10:25 UTC — Validations: spot checks of sample flows, KV cache consistency verified
- 10:40 UTC — Customer-facing status updated and replay offer posted

Customer decision cookbook (choices and steps to offer):
Option A — Opt into customer-initiated replay (recommended if your app needs bit-for-bit reconstruction):
  - What it does: Redwood will re-run requests from stored request timestamps where available and produce regenerated outputs using the recovered model variant.
  - How to request: reply to your account rep or open CS ticket with header "REPLAY REQUEST: <tenant-id> <time range>". Include sample request_id(s) if available.
  - Caveats: replays consume credits and are best-effort for very old requests beyond our short retention window. We will attach a verification digest.

Option B — Pin to prior model version (quick stopgap):
  - What it does: For customers who pin model versions in their config, pinning reverts routing to a validated variant until we finish extended verification. Low fracture risk; immediate effect.
  - How to request: change pin in Console (if available) or ask CS to apply tenant pin.
  - Caveats: pinned models may have slightly different quality/cost characteristics; test before committing at scale.

Option C — Accept short degraded-mode (latency-optimized path):
  - What it does: Switches your route to the low-latency execution path (shorter attention window, more aggressive batching). Useful for interactive apps tolerant of slight output brevity.
  - How to request: Console toggle or CS ticket "DEGRADED-MODE ON for <tenant-id>".
  - Caveats: may truncate very long completions or reduce answer richness.

Option D — Request verification bundle (for audits / legal):
  - What it includes: timestamped log extracts, per-request token counts, model variant IDs, SHA256 digests of regenerated outputs and sampling seeds where applicable.
  - How to request: CS ticket with header "VERIFICATION BUNDLE: <tenant-id>".

Status snippets customers can copy to internal stakeholders (short):
- Investigating: "Redwood is investigating intermittent truncation and latency in us-west-2. We have temporarily routed affected requests to a stable model variant and will provide an ETA."
- Actionable update: "We deployed a targeted fix to kernel selection; rolling validations underway. If you need deterministic replays, submit a replay request to your account team."
- All clear: "Issue resolved; system monitoring normal. If you experienced degraded outputs, please request a replay or verification bundle."

Suggested subject lines for customer emails:
- "Incident update — partial inference degradation in us-west-2 (07/18)"
- "Action: Request replay or model pin after resolution"
- "Verification bundle ready for <tenant-name> — follow-up required"

One-paragraph postmortem summary for customers (to paste into final status page):
Root cause: An interaction between aggressive KV cache eviction and a new kernel-selection path caused an elevated error surface for long-context requests leading to truncated outputs and higher token-latency. Impact: ~0.8% of requests routed via the affected pool experienced truncation or extended latency for a 1h window in us-west-2. Remediation: We deployed a kernel-selection flag rollback and adjusted cache eviction thresholds; long-term fix includes a safeguard in the selection logic and expanded canary coverage for long-context flows. No customer data leakage detected.

Verification checklist for customers (what we provide and how to confirm):
- Timestamped event log for your tenant (we provide start/end markers)
- Model variant IDs before/after routing change
- Sample regenerated outputs + SHA256 digests
- Operator verification notes (spot-checks used during validation)
How customers can verify locally: compare your own request IDs and timestamps to our digest bundle; run a sample reprocessing of 1–5 requests and confirm digests match.

Operator play quick-reference (internal use; paste into concise status updates):
- 1) Run targeted routing to fallback-model for the affected route
- 2) Toggle kernel-selection flag off for implicated canary hosts
- 3) Re-run 20 sample flows across pinned customer configs
- 4) Publish customer-facing status with clear action choices (replay/pin/degraded-mode)
- 5) Offer verification bundle when customers request auditable evidence

Examples: canned messages to paste into status page or email (short):
- Immediate (post alert): "We are investigating elevated latency and truncated outputs affecting a subset of requests in us-west-2. Engineers are triaging; next update in 30–60 minutes."
- Mid (after mitigation started): "Mitigated: traffic routing adjusted to a stable variant; latency metrics improving. If you saw incorrect outputs, request a replay and we will prioritize."
- Final (postmortem brief): "Resolved: fix verified and health metrics are normal. We documented cause and deployed a preventative change; replay and verification bundles are available on request."

FAQ (short):
Q: Will I lose data or tokens?
A: No customer data was exposed. Token accounting is unchanged; replays are charged per normal usage unless otherwise credited by commercial team.

Q: How long until replays complete?
A: Small replays (hundreds of requests) typically complete within hours; large replays are scheduled and may take 24–72 hours depending on scope.

Q: Can we get a credit?
A: Account teams will evaluate on a case-by-case basis for material impact. Use the CS ticket with subject "CREDIT REVIEW: <tenant-id>".

Next steps for CS/ops before publishing to customers:
- Confirm sample validations (operator sign-off)
- Prepare per-tenant replay pricing estimate where applicable
- Draft verification bundle and attach to ticket
- Send brief to account rep with recommended choice (A–D) and suggested messaging

Notes / open questions (working items):
- Add per-tenant guidance for high-throughput streaming customers (we need a small appendix)
- Consider a Console UX affordance for a one-click "request replay" that opens pre-filled CS ticket
- Decide on standard replay retention window to communicate in all postmortems

Owner notes: Maya T. — keep this lightweight. If we use, prefer short-form status snippets and the four-option cookbook rather than long narrative. This doc is meant to be editable by account teams per customer.

-- end --
